mainTopic: Fetal טבילה, lineage of mixed converts, and the permanent ban on ממזרים and נתינים
overview: This amud first finishes a question about a pregnant woman who converts. The womb fully covers the fetus, so why isn't it a barrier (חציצה) to its טבילה? The גמרא answers that the womb is the fetus's natural place of growth. Next, רבי יוחנן teaches that among non-Jews a child follows the father, but after conversion the child follows the more flawed parent. The case is an עמוני man married to a מצרית woman: a son is עמוני and a daughter is מצרית. A new משנה then rules that ממזרים and נתינים are forbidden forever, men and women alike. ריש לקיש permits a ממזרת after ten generations, and the גמרא explains this as a disagreement over how far a גזירה שוה reaches. The גמרא also teaches that a hidden ממזר does not survive, while a known one does. Finally, it begins the story of how דוד came to decree against the גבעונים during a three-year famine, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב כהנא: a full covering is a barrier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the mother's body is not a barrier for the fetus. רב כהנא taught that something covering the whole body is a חציצה, even if the person does not care about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב כהנא say that the rule (a thing you don't care about is not a barrier) applies only when it covers most of the body? If it covers all of it, it is a barrier!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous idea that the fetus counts as immersed through its mother. It quotes רב כהנא, who says a total covering always blocks טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, something a person does not mind having on him is not a חציצה. רב כהנא limits that leniency to a thing covering only most of the body. The mother's body covers the fetus completely, so by his rule it should be a barrier.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say: introduces a contradicting statement
Most of it (most of his body)
Is a barrier (blocks the water during immersion)

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Kahana say:
They only taught this about most of [his body],
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule that something a person doesn't mind is not a barrier in the מקוה.

phrases.english: but [if it covers] all of it, it is a barrier!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim (before this section) that the fetus's טבילה happens through its mother's.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the mother's body is not a חציצה for the fetus.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The womb covers the fetus entirely, and רב כהנא says a full covering is a barrier even if no one minds it.

steps.title: A fetus is different: this is how it grows
steps.stepSummary: The womb is the fetus's natural place of growth, so it is not counted as a barrier.
steps.simpleTranslation: A fetus is different, because this is the natural way it grows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A fetus inside its mother is not like a person with something stuck on him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא's rule is about outside objects that cover a body. The womb is not an outside object; it is where the fetus naturally belongs and develops. So it does not count as a חציצה at all, and the fetus is considered immersed.

phrases.english: A fetus is different,
because this is [the way of] its growth.
phrases.notes: He means the womb is the fetus's natural home, so it isn't a "covering" at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי עוּבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the case is different from the one רב כהנא was talking about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The womb is like any other full covering, so it should be a חציצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The womb is the fetus's natural place of growth, so it is not a barrier.
steps.whatToRemember: A fetus's natural place in the womb is not a חציצה, so it counts as immersed together with its mother.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: lineage among nations and after conversion
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports רבי יוחנן's rule. Among non-Jews, follow the father. After conversion, follow the more flawed parent.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבינא came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: among the nations, follow the male. If they converted, follow the more flawed of the two parents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how a child's family status is decided when the parents come from different nations. רבי יוחנן gives two rules, which the גמרא will explain one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate situations. While the parents are still non-Jews, the child is counted as part of the father's nation. Once the parents have become גרים, the child takes the status of whichever parent has the more problematic lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: When [so-and-so] came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
The more flawed of the two

phrases.english: When Ravina came,
[he said that] Rabbi Yochanan said:
Among the nations, follow the male.
If they converted, follow the more flawed of the two.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִינָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, not connected to the fetus discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Non-Jewish lineage follows the father; after conversion, the child follows the more flawed parent.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule decides whether a child of mixed parents may marry into the Jewish people, and whether he counts as a כנעני.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא: a son of a Canaanite mother may be bought
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a son born to a non-Canaanite father and a Canaanite mother may be bought as a slave. So the child follows his father, not his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Among the nations, follow the male," as a ברייתא teaches. How do we know that if a man from the nations fathers a son with a Canaanite woman, you may buy him as a slave? Because the פסוק says: "And also from the children of the residents who live with you, from them you may buy."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first rule by bringing a ברייתא. The son of a Canaanite mother is not treated as a Canaanite, because his father isn't one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כנעני is not allowed to stay in ארץ ישראל, so one could not buy him as a slave and keep him there. The ברייתא allows buying the son of a Canaanite mother and a non-Canaanite father. That shows the mother's nation does not decide; the father's does.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Allowed to buy him as a slave

phrases.english: "Among the nations, follow the male,"
as it is taught [in a baraita]:
From where [do we know] that one from the nations
who had relations with a Canaanite woman and fathered a son,
that you are permitted to buy him as a slave?
phrases.notes: A כנעני can't be kept in ארץ ישראל, so being allowed to buy him means he isn't counted as a כנעני.

phrases.english: As it is said:
"And also from the children of the residents who live with you,
from them you may buy."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:45

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאוּמּוֹת הַלֵּךְ אַחַר הַזָּכָר, כִּדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the first half of רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.raayaObject: באומות הלך אחר הזכר: among the nations, follow the father.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 25:45: the son of a non-Canaanite father and a Canaanite mother may be bought.

steps.title: The other side: a son of a Canaanite father may not be bought
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A son of a Canaanite father and a non-Canaanite mother may not be bought, because he follows his Canaanite father.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that even a son of a Canaanite man and a woman from another nation may be bought as a slave. So the פסוק says "which they fathered in your land": from those born in your land, and not from those who came to live in your land.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the proof from the other direction. When the father is the Canaanite, the son is a Canaanite and may not be bought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "born in your land" point to a child whose mother is the Canaanite, since a woman normally stays in her own land. A man who came in from outside may be the son of a Canaanite father, and he is excluded. Together the two halves show that the father alone decides the child's nation.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (to rule that out)
Those living (who came to live) in your land

phrases.english: One might think that even one of the Canaanites

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבָּא עַל אַחַת מִן הָאוּמּוֹת וְהוֹלִיד בֵּן,
phrases.english: who had relations with a woman from the nations and fathered a son,
that you are permitted to buy him as a slave;
therefore the verse teaches:
"which they fathered in your land":
from those born in your land,
and not from those living in your land.
phrases.notes: Someone born here has a local Canaanite mother; someone who moved in from outside might have a Canaanite father.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ אֶחָד מִן הַכְּנַעֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: Lineage among the nations follows the father.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words "אשר הולידו בארצכם" exclude the son of a Canaanite father.
steps.whatToRemember: Among non-Jews, the father decides the child's nation. A Canaanite mother does not make the child a כנעני, but a Canaanite father does.

steps.title: Which case is 'the more flawed of the two' about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second half of רבי יוחנן's rule and asks what case it refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: "If they converted, follow the more flawed of the two." In what case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the second rule and asks which couple it is talking about. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule only makes sense if both parents have some kind of flaw that can be compared. The גמרא is looking for a pair of גרים where this is true.

phrases.english: "If they converted, follow the more flawed of the two."
In what [case]?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְגַּיְּירוּ הַלֵּךְ אַחַר פָּגוּם שֶׁבִּשְׁנֵיהֶם. בְּמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the second half of the מימרא in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which couple of converts the rule of "the more flawed of the two" is about.

steps.title: Not an Egyptian man with an Ammonite woman
steps.stepSummary: The rule can't be about an מצרי man who married an עמונית woman, because an Ammonite woman has no flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means an Egyptian man who married an Ammonite woman, what "more flawed" is there with her? The תורה said "an Ammonite" (man), not an Ammonite woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one possible case and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's ban on עמוני applies only to men; an עמונית may marry into the Jewish people right away. In this couple, only the Egyptian father has a flaw. There is nothing to compare, so the phrase "the more flawed of the two" wouldn't fit.

keyTerms.meaning: An Ammonite man, but not an Ammonite woman

phrases.english: If you say [it is about] an Egyptian man who married an Ammonite woman,
what "more flawed of the two" is there in her?
[The Torah says] "Ammonite," but not an Ammonite woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא בְּמִצְרִי שֶׁנָּשָׂא עַמּוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the שאלה and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this one proposed case, not רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An עמונית has no flaw at all, so there is nothing to call "more flawed."
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think every Ammonite convert is barred. The ban is only on Ammonite men; women are permitted.

steps.title: The case: an Ammonite man with an Egyptian woman
steps.stepSummary: The rule is about an עמוני man who married a מצרית woman. A son follows his Ammonite father, and a daughter follows her Egyptian mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about an Ammonite man who married an Egyptian woman. If the child is a male, assign him to the Ammonite. If it is a female, assign her to the Egyptian.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct case and shows how "follow the more flawed" works for sons and for daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both parents have a flaw. A son follows his עמוני father, which is the worse status for him: permanently barred. A daughter would be fully permitted as an עמונית, so she follows her מצרית mother, which is the worse status for her. She counts as a second-generation Egyptian.

keyTerms.meaning: Cast him after (assign him the status of)

phrases.english: Rather, [it is about] an Ammonite man who married an Egyptian woman.
If it is a male,
assign him after the Ammonite [father];
if it is a female,
assign her after the Egyptian [mother].
phrases.notes: So she is treated like a second-generation Egyptian; only the third generation may marry in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּעַמּוֹנִי שֶׁנָּשָׂא מִצְרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct case after step 7 rejected the first suggestion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עמוני man married to a מצרית woman: a son takes the Ammonite status, and a daughter takes the Egyptian status.
steps.whatToRemember: After conversion, "follow the more flawed" means each child gets the stricter status that applies to that child. A son is Ammonite (permanently barred); a daughter is Egyptian (second generation).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that "more flawed" depends on the child's gender, since the Ammonite ban applies only to males.

steps.title: ממזרים and נתינים are forbidden forever, males and females alike
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that ממזרים and נתינים may never marry into the community, and this applies to both men and women.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: ממזרים and נתינים are forbidden, and their prohibition lasts forever. This applies to both males and females.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says ממזרים and נתינים are forbidden to marry a born Jew forever, and women are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we saw that with עמוני and מואבי only the men are forbidden, and with Egyptians the ban ends after a few generations. This משנה says neither of those limits applies here. The ban is permanent and covers women too.

keyTerms.meaning: Children born from a forbidden union, such as incest or adultery
The Gibeonites, who converted in the days of יהושע

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Mamzerim and Gibeonites are forbidden,
phrases.notes: Forbidden to marry a woman who was born Jewish.

phrases.english: and their prohibition is forever.
Both males and females.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַמְזֵרִין וּנְתִינִין אֲסוּרִין, וְאִיסּוּרָן אִיסּוּר עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of עמוני and מצרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ממזרים and נתינים are forbidden forever, both males and females.

steps.title: A ממזרת is permitted after ten generations
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that a ממזרת may marry into the community after ten generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: ריש לקיש said: A ממזרת is permitted after ten generations.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a rule that seems to limit the משנה. After ten generations, a female descendant of a ממזר is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the ban on females lasts forever. ריש לקיש says that for females it ends after ten generations. The next step gives his source.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Reish Lakish said:
A female mamzer is permitted after ten generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מַמְזֶרֶת לְאַחַר עֲשָׂרָה דּוֹרוֹת מוּתֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An אמורא's ruling that seems to conflict with the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ממזרת is permitted after ten generations.

steps.title: Learning from the word 'tenth' in the verses about Ammonites and Moabites
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns a גזירה שוה from the word 'tenth' in both verses. Since Ammonite and Moabite women are permitted, a ממזרת is permitted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'tenth' and 'tenth' from עמוני and מואבי. Just as there, females are permitted, so too here, females are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where ריש לקיש got his rule. He uses a גזירה שוה, a link between two verses that use the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the ממזר verse and the עמוני/מואבי verse say 'even to the tenth generation.' With עמוני and מואבי, the women are not included in the ban. ריש לקיש carries that over and says a ממזרת is also permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both
There, meaning the other case we are learning from
Here, meaning the case we are discussing

phrases.english: He learns "tenth" "tenth"
phrases.notes: Both פסוקים say 'even to the tenth generation': דברים 23:3 for a ממזר and דברים 23:4 for עמוני ומואבי.

phrases.english: from Ammonite and Moabite.
Just as there, females are permitted,
so too here, females are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָלֵיף עֲשִׂירִי עֲשִׂירִי מֵעַמּוֹנִי וּמוֹאָבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That a ממזרת is permitted after ten generations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on the word 'tenth' from עמוני and מואבי, where females are permitted.

steps.title: Then she should be permitted right away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the comparison. Ammonite women are permitted immediately, so a ממזרת should be permitted immediately too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there they are permitted immediately, so too here she should be permitted immediately!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on ריש לקיש's comparison. Why should she wait ten generations?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An Ammonite woman may marry into the community from the first generation. If the ממזרת is learned from her, the comparison should make the ממזרת permitted at once, not after ten generations.

phrases.english: If so: just as there, immediately,
so too here, immediately!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי: מָה לְהַלָּן מִיָּד, אַף כָּאן מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the גזירה שוה from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ten-generation limit in ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is to Ammonite women, it should give the ממזרת their full law, which is being permitted immediately.

steps.title: The analogy only works from the tenth generation on
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה is built on the word 'tenth,' so it only applies from the tenth generation and onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גזירה שוה only takes effect from the tenth generation and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The comparison only starts working from the tenth generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link between the two verses is the word 'tenth.' So the comparison only applies from the point that word marks, the tenth generation. Before that, the ממזרת is still forbidden.

phrases.english: When the verbal analogy takes effect,
it is from the tenth and onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַהֲנִי גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, מֵעֲשִׂירִי וְאֵילָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits how far the גזירה שוה reaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ממזרת should get the Ammonite woman's full law and be permitted immediately.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה only works from the tenth generation, the point its key word refers to.

steps.title: But the משנה says females are forbidden forever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש from our משנה, which says the ban is forever for both males and females.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: ממזרים and נתינים are forbidden, their prohibition is forever, both males and females!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our משנה against ריש לקיש. The משנה says the women are forbidden forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said a ממזרת becomes permitted after ten generations. The משנה clearly says the ban on females never ends. That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
Mamzerim and Gibeonites are forbidden,
and their prohibition is forever,
both males and females!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאֲנַן תְּנַן: מַמְזֵרִים וּנְתִינִין אֲסוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to ריש לקיש, this time from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that a ממזרת is permitted after ten generations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says the ban on females is forever.

steps.title: ריש לקיש follows the opinion of 'learn from it fully'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש follows the תנא who holds דון מינה ומינה. Our משנה follows a different opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. ריש לקיש's view follows the one who says 'learn from it, and from it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is a known disagreement. ריש לקיש sides with one opinion, and our משנה follows the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under דון מינה ומינה, once you compare two cases, you carry over the other case's details too. So even though the verse is mainly about forbidding the ממזר, it also teaches that the ממזרת is permitted after ten generations, like Ammonite women. The משנה follows a תנא who does not stretch the comparison this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it fully, carrying over all of its details

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש permits a ממזרת after ten generations through a גזירה שוה on the word 'tenth.' It works only from the tenth generation on, and it follows the opinion of דון מינה ומינה. Our משנה, which forbids females forever, follows the other view.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the משנה is wrong. It answers that the משנה follows a different תנא than the one ריש לקיש follows.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This follows the one who says
"Learn from it, and from it."
phrases.notes: Once you compare one case to another, you bring over that case's details too, not just the main point.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר דּוּן מִינַּהּ וּמִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a dispute among תנאים. ריש לקיש follows one side and the משנה follows the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה rules out ריש לקיש's view completely.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש follows the opinion of דון מינה ומינה, which carries the details of the Ammonite law over to the ממזרת.

steps.title: Our משנה follows the 'learn it and keep it in its place' method
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: our משנה follows the opinion of דון מינה ואוקי באתרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: That opinion (our משנה) follows the one who says: learn from it, and then leave it in its own place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its answer from the last step by naming the method our משנה uses. It explains why our משנה, unlike ריש לקיש, forbids female ממזרים forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש uses דון מינה ומינה: once you link two cases, you copy all the details, including that women are permitted. Our משנה uses דון מינה ואוקי באתרא: you borrow only the main point (the 'tenth generation' means forever), and the ממזר case keeps its own rules. Since the ממזר ban has no exception for women, a ממזרת stays forbidden forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, and keep it in its place: borrow only the main rule, not every detail
Like the one who says (follows that opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to use a גזירה שוה: דון מינה ומינה (copy everything) gives ריש לקיש's view, and דון מינה ואוקי באתרא (copy only the main rule) gives our משנה's view.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the same גזירה שוה from the word 'tenth.' They disagree only about how much of the other case you are allowed to copy over.

phrases.english: That one is like the one who says:
phrases.notes: 'That one' is our משנה, which forbids female ממזרים forever.

phrases.english: Learn from it, and set it in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְּאַתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part answer of step 15 by naming our משנה's method.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different תנאים: the two sources follow different methods of applying a גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seemed to disprove ריש לקיש outright.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows דון מינה ואוקי באתרא, so it does not contradict ריש לקיש, who follows דון מינה ומינה.

steps.title: Students ask about a ממזרת after ten generations
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי אליעזר what the law is for a ממזרת after ten generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי אליעזר: A ממזרת after ten generations, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story where students ask רבי אליעזר whether a ממזרת becomes permitted after ten generations. This sets up his surprising answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question connects to ריש לקיש's idea that a ממזרת may be permitted from the tenth generation on. The students want to know whether such a woman can marry into the community.

phrases.english: They asked Rabbi Eliezer:
A mamzeret after ten generations, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate over the גזירה שוה to a real question about a ממזרת after ten generations.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a ממזרת permitted to marry into the community after ten generations?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: find me even a third generation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that he wishes he could even find a third-generation ממזר to declare pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Who would give me a third generation, and I would declare him pure!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר does not answer about ten generations at all. He says he cannot even find a ממזר family that has reached the third generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer means the question is not practical: you will never actually meet a tenth-generation ממזרת. The גמרא will explain why in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Who would give me (if only I had)
And I would declare him pure

phrases.english: He said to them:
Who would give me a third generation
and I would declare him pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי יִתֵּן לִי דּוֹר שְׁלִישִׁי וַאֲטַהֲרֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question by sidestepping it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case never comes up, since he cannot even find a third-generation ממזר.

steps.title: A ממזר does not survive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from רבי אליעזר that a ממזר does not survive, and רב הונא says the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Apparently he holds that a ממזר does not live. And so said רב הונא: a ממזר does not live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's answer: he holds that ממזרים do not survive for many generations. It then shows that רב הונא holds this too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is why you can never find a third-generation ממזר: the line does not last. רב הונא's matching statement gives this idea a second source.

keyTerms.meaning: A ממזר does not live (does not survive)

phrases.english: Apparently he holds
a mamzer does not live.
And so said Rav Huna:
a mamzer does not live.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר מַמְזֵרָא לָא חָיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the principle behind רבי אליעזר's answer and supports it with רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ממזר does not survive over the generations.

steps.title: But the משנה says the ban is forever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: our משנה says ממזרים are forbidden forever, which assumes their families last.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: ממזרים are forbidden, and their prohibition is forever!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that a ממזר does not survive, using the words of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ממזר families die out within three generations, why does the משנה need to say the ban lasts forever? Its words assume ממזרים keep having descendants.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
Mamzerim are forbidden,
and their prohibition is a forever prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן מַמְזֵרִין אֲסוּרִין וְאִיסּוּרָן אִיסּוּר עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle stated in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that ממזרא לא חיי (רבי אליעזר and רב הונא).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A forever ban only makes sense if ממזר families continue for many generations.

steps.title: It depends on whether the ממזר is known
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, from רב יהודה: a known ממזר lives, an unknown one does not, and a suspected one lasts up to three generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: רב יהודה himself explained it to me. One who is known lives. One who is not known does not live. One who is known and not known lives up to three generations; more than that, he does not live.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge by splitting ממזרים into three groups based on how well known their status is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's 'forever' ban is about a known ממזר, whose family does survive. The rule that a ממזר does not live is about one whose status is hidden. A suspected ממזר is in between: up to three generations, which fits רבי אליעזר's 'third generation.'

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally

steps.whatToRemember: Known ממזר: survives, so the 'forever' ban applies. Hidden ממזר: does not survive. Suspected ממזר: up to three generations.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Does not live' does not mean every ממזר dies. A known ממזר survives. An unknown one does not, and a suspected one lasts only up to three generations.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
To me, it was explained to me
by Rav Yehuda himself:
One who is known lives,
one who is not known does not live.
One who is known and not known
phrases.notes: Someone people suspect is a ממזר, but no one is sure.

phrases.english: lives up to three generations,
more than that, does not live.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between step 19 and the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the משנה and רב הונא are talking about different kinds of ממזר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that no ממזר family survives, which would make the משנה's 'forever' pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: A known ממזר survives, so the forever ban applies to him; only an unknown ממזר does not survive.

steps.title: רבי אמי: 'I have given you life'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי announced that a neighbor was a ממזר, and when the man cried, told him he had given him life.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain man in רבי אמי's neighborhood. רבי אמי announced about him that he was a ממזר. The man went around crying. רבי אמי said to him: I have given you life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רב יהודה's rule in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being publicly declared a ממזר felt like a disaster to the man. But by the rule just taught, once a ממזר is known he survives, so the announcement actually saved his life.
steps.whatToRemember: The story makes the rule concrete: a ממזר whose status is known will survive.

phrases.english: A certain man who was
in the neighborhood of Rabbi Ami.
He announced about him that he was a mamzer.
He went about crying.
He said to him:
I have given you life.
phrases.notes: Now that he is a known ממזר, by רב יהודה's rule he will survive.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דְּהָוֵי בְּשִׁבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule from step 21 in action.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making a ממזר's status public gives him life, since a known ממזר survives.

steps.title: דוד made the decree against the גבעונים
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר אדא says the ban on marrying נתינים comes from a decree of דוד, and brings a פסוק about the גבעונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר אדא said: The נתינים were banned by a decree of דוד. As the פסוק says: "The king called the גבעונים and spoke to them. The גבעונים are not from בני ישראל."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement explaining who first banned the נתינים from marrying into the Jewish people. רב חנא בר אדא says it was דוד המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said נתינים are forbidden forever, but did not say where the ban comes from. רב חנא בר אדא points to a פסוק where דוד calls the גבעונים "not from בני ישראל". He reads this as דוד ruling that they may not join the קהל, even though they had converted.

keyTerms.meaning: The גבעונים, who joined the Jewish people in יהושע's time and were later banned from marrying in
The people of גבעון, the same group as the נתינים
He made a decree against them

steps.confusionAlert: The words נתינים and גבעונים refer to the same group. The גמרא calls them נתינים, while the פסוק calls them גבעונים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us the ban on נתינים comes from a decree of דוד. It is not stated directly in the תורה, and the rest of the story explains why he made it.

phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Adda said:
The Gibeonites: David made a decree against them,
phrases.notes: He means דוד is the one who banned them from marrying into the Jewish people.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "And the king called the Gibeonites
and said to them

phrases.aramaic: וְהַגִּבְעוֹנִים לֹא מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵמָּה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: Now the Gibeonites are not of the children of Israel, etc."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:2

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר אַדָּא: נְתִינִים — דָּוִד גָּזַר עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ממזרים to the other group the משנה calls forbidden forever, the נתינים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on נתינים comes from a decree of דוד המלך.

steps.title: Why did דוד make this decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason דוד had for banning the גבעונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the reason he made a decree against them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why דוד banned the גבעונים. This short question sets up the long story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know who made the decree, but not why. The answer is a whole story, which begins in the next step.

phrases.english: What is the reason he decreed against them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא גְּזַר עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the decree mentioned in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What led דוד to ban the גבעונים from joining the קהל.

steps.title: The famine begins and idol worship is checked first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts the answer with the three-year famine in דוד's time. In the first year, דוד suspected idol worship. They checked and found none.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: "There was a famine in the days of דוד for three years, year after year." In the first year, דוד said to them: "Maybe there are idol worshippers among you," as the פסוק says: "You will serve other gods and bow to them... and He will close the heavens and there will be no rain." They checked, and found none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer the question by telling the story of a three-year famine. In the first year, דוד checked whether people were worshipping idols, since the תורה links that sin to lack of rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד treated the famine as a punishment and looked for its cause. He started with עבודה זרה, because a פסוק in דברים says it stops the rain. The search found nothing, so the cause must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: They checked and did not find (anyone guilty)

phrases.english: As it is written: "And there was a famine in the days of David
three years, year after year."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:1

phrases.english: In the first year he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יֵשׁ בָּכֶם,
phrases.english: Perhaps there are idol worshippers among you,
as it is written: "And you serve other gods
and bow down to them.
And He will shut up the heavens
and there will be no rain, etc."
They checked, and did not find any.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי רָעָב בִּימֵי דָוִד שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים שָׁנָה אַחַר שָׁנָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question from step 24 by telling the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer starts with the famine story. The first suspected cause, idol worship, was checked and ruled out.

steps.title: Second year: forbidden relationships are checked
steps.stepSummary: In the second year, דוד suspected sexual sins, based on a פסוק in ירמיהו. They checked and found none.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the second year, he said to them: "Maybe there are people among you who commit forbidden relations," as the פסוק says: "The showers were held back, and there was no late rain, yet you had the forehead of a זונה." They checked, and found none.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. In the second year of famine, דוד checked whether people were committing forbidden relationships.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו links shameless immoral behavior with rain being held back. That makes it the next possible cause. Again nothing was found, so the search goes on.

keyTerms.meaning: Sinners; here, people committing forbidden relations

phrases.english: In the second year he said to them:
Perhaps there are transgressors among you,
as it is written: "And the showers were withheld
and there was no late rain,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵצַח אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה הָיָה לָךְ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: yet you had the forehead of a harlot, etc."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:3

phrases.english: They checked, and did not find any.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנִיָּה אָמַר לָהֶם: שֶׁמָּא עוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה יֵשׁ בָּכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the famine story into the second year, checking a second possible sin.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second suspected cause, forbidden relationships, was checked and ruled out.

steps.title: Third year: false charity pledges are checked
steps.stepSummary: In the third year, דוד suspected people who publicly promise צדקה but never give it, based on a פסוק in משלי. They checked and found none.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the third year, he said to them: "Maybe there are people among you who promise צדקה in public and then don't give it," as the פסוק says: "Clouds and wind, but no rain: a man who boasts of a gift he never gives." They checked, and found none.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues into the third year. דוד checked whether people were publicly promising צדקה and then not paying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in משלי compares someone who boasts of a fake gift to clouds and wind that bring no rain. So empty charity pledges are another possible cause of drought. This search also failed, which sets up the real cause in the continuation of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: A false gift, one promised but never given

steps.confusionAlert: The story is not over. Three different sins were checked and none was found. The real cause, which connects to the גבעונים, comes next.

phrases.english: In the third year he said to them:
Perhaps those who pledge charity in public
are among you, and do not actually give,
as it is written: "Vapors and wind
and there is no rain:
a man who boasts of a false gift."
phrases.notes: משלי 25:14

phrases.english: They checked, and did not find any.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלִישִׁית אָמַר לָהֶם: שֶׁמָּא פּוֹסְקֵי צְדָקָה בָּרַבִּים יֵשׁ בָּכֶם וְאֵין נוֹתְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the famine story into the third year, checking a third possible sin.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The third suspected cause, unpaid public charity pledges, was checked and ruled out. This leaves the real cause still to be found.

steps.title: דוד realizes the problem depends on him
steps.stepSummary: Having found no sin among the people, דוד concludes the famine must be connected to himself, and he immediately seeks ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: The matter depends only on me. Immediately: "And דוד sought the presence of ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The story of the famine continues. After three years of checking the people and finding nothing, דוד decides the cause must be connected to him as the leader, so he turns to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 25-27 ruled out the sins of the people one by one. Since nothing was found there, דוד looks to the leadership instead. This sets up the question of how exactly he 'sought' ה׳.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אֵין הַדָּבָר תָּלוּי אֶלָּא בִּי,
phrases.english: He said: The matter depends only on me,
phrases.notes: 'He' is דוד.

phrases.english: Immediately: "And David sought the presence of the Lord."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:1

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: אֵין הַדָּבָר תָּלוּי אֶלָּא בִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the elimination process of steps 25-27 and moves the search to דוד himself.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With the people cleared, דוד turns to ה׳ to learn the cause.

steps.title: How did דוד seek ה׳?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק means by saying דוד 'sought the presence of ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about the פסוק just quoted: what was this 'seeking'? It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'sought the presence of ה׳' are vague. They could mean prayer, or something else. The גמרא wants to know the actual method.

keyTerms.meaning: what is this? (what does it refer to?)

phrases.english: What is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the פסוק quoted in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What form did דוד's 'seeking the presence of ה׳' take?

steps.title: He asked through the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that דוד asked ה׳ through the אורים ותומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: He asked through the אורים ותומים.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers that דוד's 'seeking' means he asked a question through the אורים ותומים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So this was not just a general prayer. It was a formal question to ה׳ that received an answer through the כהן גדול's breastplate. This explains how ה׳ 'answers' in the next part of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: the stones of the כהן גדול's breastplate, used to ask ה׳ questions

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
That he asked through the Urim VeTummim.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: שֶׁשָּׁאַל בְּאוּרִים וְתוּמִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דוד inquired through the אורים ותומים.

steps.title: Where do we see that from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know from the פסוק that the 'seeking' was through the אורים ותומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of ריש לקיש's claim. It is setting up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק never mentions the אורים ותומים. So the גמרא wants to know what in the wording points to them.

keyTerms.meaning: from where is it implied? (what shows this?)

phrases.english: From where is it implied?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual source of step 30's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the פסוק shows that the אורים ותומים were used?

steps.title: Learning it from the word 'presence' in both verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר derives it through a גזירה שוה: the word ״פני״ appears here and also in a פסוק that explicitly speaks about the אורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: We learn ״פני״ from ״פני״. It is written here: "And דוד sought the presence of ה׳," and it is written there: "He shall ask for him by the judgment of the אורים before ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר proves ריש לקיש's point by matching the word ״פני״ in our פסוק to the same word in a פסוק about asking with the אורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In במדבר, ״לפני ה׳״ is used for asking through the אורים. Because the same word ״פני״ appears in דוד's story, we read it the same way: דוד asked through the אורים ותומים.

keyTerms.meaning: it comes (is learned) — used for a גזירה שוה
it is written here... and it is written there
by the judgment of the אורים

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
It is learned from "presence" and "presence."
phrases.notes: The same word appears in two פסוקים, so we learn the meaning of one from the other.

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״וַיְבַקֵּשׁ דָּוִד אֶת פְּנֵי ה׳״,
phrases.english: It is written here: "And David sought the presence of the Lord,"
And it is written there:
"Who shall inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim before the Lord."
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:21

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתְיָא ״פְּנֵי״ ״פְּנֵי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 31 with a גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shared word ״פני״ links דוד's seeking to inquiry through the אורים.

steps.title: ה׳'s answer: שאול's הספד and the גבעונים
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק gives ה׳'s answer, and the גמרא explains it as two separate reasons: שאול was not eulogized properly, and his house is blamed for killing the גבעונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And ה׳ said: For שאול and for the house of blood, because he killed the גבעונים." "For שאול" — because he was not eulogized properly. "And for the house of blood" — "because he killed the גבעונים."
steps.whatsHappening: Now we hear ה׳'s answer through the אורים, and the גמרא splits it into two reasons for the famine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "For שאול" is one reason: שאול did not get a proper הספד. "The house of blood" is a second reason: the killing of the גבעונים. This is the first time the גבעונים enter the story, which leads toward why דוד decreed against them.

keyTerms.meaning: the גבעונים, the people of גבעון

phrases.english: "And the Lord said: For Saul,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:1

phrases.english: And for the house of blood,
Because he put to death the Gibeonites."
"For Saul" — because he was not eulogized properly,
"And for the house of blood" —
"Because he put to death the Gibeonites."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֶל שָׁאוּל וְאֶל בֵּית הַדָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer דוד received through the אורים ותומים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The famine came for two reasons: שאול's missing הספד, and the killing of the גבעונים.

steps.title: Where did שאול ever kill the גבעונים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we ever find that שאול killed the גבעונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where do we find that שאול killed the גבעונים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the פסוק's claim, because no story in תנ״ך tells of שאול killing the גבעונים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation in step 33 rests on שאול having killed the גבעונים. If no such event exists, the reading seems to have no basis.

phrases.english: But where do we find regarding Saul
That he put to death the Gibeonites?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הֵיכָן מָצִינוּ בְּשָׁאוּל שֶׁהֵמִית הַגִּבְעוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual basis of step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שאול killed the גבעונים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No story in תנ״ך records שאול killing the גבעונים.

steps.title: Destroying נוב counts as killing the גבעונים
steps.stepSummary: Because שאול destroyed נוב, the city of כהנים that supplied the גבעונים with water and food, the פסוק counts it as if he killed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because he killed נוב, the city of כהנים, who used to supply them with water and food, the פסוק considers it as if he killed them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שאול did not kill the גבעונים directly. He destroyed their source of food and water, so it counts as if he killed them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גבעונים depended on the כהנים of נוב for their food and water. When שאול wiped out נוב, he cut off their support, and the פסוק blames him as if he had killed them himself.

keyTerms.meaning: נוב, the city of the כהנים, which שאול destroyed
the פסוק considers it on him

phrases.english: Rather, because he killed
Nob, the city of the priests,
Who used to supply them with water and food,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the גבעונים. The כהנים of נוב were feeding them.

phrases.english: The verse regards it as if he killed them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהָרַג נוֹב עִיר הַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: indirect causation counts as killing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to describe a direct killing that never happened.
steps.terutzMaskana: Destroying the גבעונים' source of food and water is counted as killing them.

steps.title: How can one פסוק both defend and accuse שאול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that ה׳ would demand honor for שאול, about his הספד, and at the same moment demand punishment for his sin against the גבעונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He demands for שאול because he was not eulogized properly, and He demands because he killed the גבעונים?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a seeming contradiction inside ה׳'s answer: one part defends שאול's honor, and the other part blames him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Complaining about שאול's missing הספד means standing up for him. Blaming him for the גבעונים means accusing him. It seems strange for both to appear in the same breath.

phrases.english: He demands on behalf of Saul
That he was not eulogized properly,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא תָבַע עַל אֲשֶׁר הֵמִית הַגִּבְעוֹנִים?!
phrases.english: And He demands because he put to death the Gibeonites?!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא תָבַע אֶל שָׁאוּל שֶׁלֹּא נִסְפַּד כַּהֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the double reading of the פסוק given in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the פסוק as both honoring and blaming שאול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Defending someone's honor and accusing him seem to contradict each other in a single answer.

steps.title: Where one is judged, his good deeds are mentioned too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says yes, both belong together, citing ריש לקיש: wherever a person's judgment is mentioned, his good deeds are mentioned there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as ריש לקיש said: What is meant by what is written: "Seek ה׳, all the humble of the land, who have done His judgment"? Where his judgment is, there his deeds are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the double reading and explains it with a teaching of ריש לקיש: when a person is judged, his good deeds are remembered alongside his sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads ״משפטו פעלו״ as 'his judgment, his deeds', meaning both are mentioned in the same place. So when ה׳ judges שאול for נוב, He also remembers שאול's merits and demands his proper honor. The contradiction disappears.
steps.whatToRemember: ה׳'s answer to דוד was twofold: שאול deserved a proper הספד, and his house was guilty for the גבעונים, whom he harmed by destroying נוב. Both appear together because when a person is judged, his good deeds are mentioned too.

phrases.english: Yes, as Reish Lakish said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Seek the Lord, all the humble of the land,
phrases.notes: צפניה 2:3

phrases.english: Who have carried out His judgment",
Where his judgment is — there are his deeds.
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש reads the words in a new way: where a person is judged, his good deeds are brought up right there too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 36 by accepting the double reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Acceptance with a supporting principle (ריש לקיש's reading of צפניה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Honoring and accusing שאול in one answer seemed contradictory.
steps.terutzMaskana: Judgment and good deeds are always mentioned together, so both belong in ה׳'s answer.

steps.title: דוד begins his response about שאול's הספד
steps.stepSummary: דוד starts to respond to the first reason ה׳ gave, that שאול was not eulogized properly, by noting that time has already passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said: Regarding שאול, there have already passed...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up דוד's reaction to ה׳'s answer. He starts by dealing with the first reason, the missing הספד for שאול, and says that time has already gone by. The sentence finishes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 33 the גמרא split ה׳'s answer into two reasons. Here דוד takes up the first one, שאול's הספד. By saying 'there have passed,' he is pointing out that a lot of time has gone by since שאול died, and the next lines will spell out how much.

keyTerms.meaning: David said: this opens דוד's reaction to ה׳'s answer
King Saul, whose eulogy is being discussed
Have already passed, gone by (said about time)

phrases.english: David said:
Regarding Saul, there have already passed
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going in the next lines, which say what has passed. דוד is starting with the first reason, the הספד.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר דָּוִד: שָׁאוּל, נְפַקוּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With both of ה׳'s reasons now explained (steps 33-37), the story returns to דוד, who begins answering the first reason, the missing הספד for שאול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד begins to point out that time has already passed since שאול's death. The full statement continues in the next lines.
